newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria calls for dialogue to end Albania crisis.
newsitem.headline: Austria calls for dialogue to end Albania crisis.

text.p: Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said on Sunday the situation in Albania was "immensely difficult" and called for a dialogue between government and opposition to overcome the country's crisis.
"We're dealing here with an immensely diffuclt and very opaque situation," Schuessel told Austrian television. "It is important to send clear signals to the government and to President Sali Berisha.
He said the government and opposition should attempt to establish a round table.

Talks between Berisha and opposition parties on ending an armed rebellion in the south of Europe's poorest country remained deadlocked after eight hours of talks on Saturday but were likely to resume on Sunday.

The West has stepped up mediation efforts as rebels maintained their hold on the south. The revolt was sparked by the collapse of five pyramid investment schemes in January which swallowed the savings of thousands of Albanians.
Schuessel criticised Berisha's government for its handling of the scandal. "The government has made serious mistakes by not putting a stop to these pyramid games," he said.

Former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky travelled to Tirana on Saturday as envoy for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in an attempt to help resolve the crisis that has engulfed Albania.

After two rounds of talks with Berisha, Vranitzky told reporters the embattled president was considering an extension of a 48-hour halt to government military action against rebels and ways of adapting his proposal for new elections.
